title: Searching for Nitrogen-Vacancy Centers in Diamond with Multislice Electron Ptychography
content: The advent of powerful quantum computers would bring about numerous advancements in quantum cryptography, artificial intelligence, and physics-based simulations. A limitation of quantum computers today is keeping states coherent across a large array of qubits. Nitrogen-vacancy centers (NV-centers) in diamond could be a solution to this problem because of their qubit properties and random formation within the diamond lattice [1]. Further development of devices based around NV-centers require the ability to precisely measure their location in three dimensions. Electron tomography already allows for 3D atomic resolution images; however, this technique requires multiple scans to be taken across a wide range of angles, which proves to be challenging experimentally and computationally [2]. Multislice electron ptychography allows for the possibility to acquire a 3D reconstruction of the sample with only one data set; thus, drastically reducing the experimental and computational complexity. The tradeoff is that the depth resolution of multislice ptychography is still on the order of a few nm [3]. Therefore, I will outline key experimental and algorithmic parameters to improve the depth resolution of multislice ptychographic reconstructions.
